I am a woman of 54 years here in Ruvuma, and my rice plot is almost one hectare. I went to school a little, so I can read the bag, but I farm the way my mother taught me and the way my neighbors do. Cash is tight this season, but rice without a little urea gives a poor harvest, so I will buy one bag of urea and put it on at top-dressing time when the rice is growing well — that is what most of us do here. I will use the seed I saved from last year because improved rice seed is expensive and the agro-dealer in Songea is far; my plot sits in a low place that floods with the rains so I do not need to pay for irrigation, and I will weed by hand with my daughter-in-law and hire a few people only for transplanting and harvest.
